title: Armored Core: Nexus
subtitle: Old technology starts another corporate war
summary: Armored Core: Nexus is FromSoftware's PlayStation 2 mecha combat game, first released in Japan on 18 March 2004. A corporation's accumulation of ancient technology destabilises the existing powers, drawing the player into missions whose consequences grow increasingly dangerous. The pilot again earns money to alter a personal Armored Core, linking the larger conflict to the machinery used to carry out each contract. Nexus continues the series after Silent Line as a full sequel. Its changes affect how the machine is handled as well as the setting in which the mercenary is asked to work.
body: Armored Core: Nexus is FromSoftware's PlayStation 2 mecha combat game, first released in Japan on 18 March 2004. A corporation's accumulation of ancient technology destabilises the existing powers, drawing the player into missions whose consequences grow increasingly dangerous. The pilot again earns money to alter a personal Armored Core, linking the larger conflict to the machinery used to carry out each contract. Nexus continues the series after Silent Line as a full sequel. Its changes affect how the machine is handled as well as the setting in which the mercenary is asked to work.

Dual-analogue support gives the player a different way to move and aim, updating a control arrangement that had remained distinctive across the earlier games. The underlying task is still to make a customised machine work in a difficult combat situation. Parts, weapons and their interactions need to be considered before the mission, then judged through the response of the machine in motion. LAN multiplayer adds another setting for those designs to meet. The new controls make the familiar systems more immediately accessible without removing the need to understand what the assembled equipment can sustain.

Rintaro Yamada directed and Toshifumi Nabeshima produced, with Kota Hoshino composing the score. Nexus pairs its new campaign with a second disc revisiting earlier series missions, giving the release both a forward movement and a retrospective element. North America received it in September 2004, with PAL editions following later. The combination makes it a useful point from which to see how Armored Core had developed. Familiar mission ideas can be encountered through revised systems, while the new corporate crisis continues the series' habit of making the mercenary's workshop part of a much larger conflict.
